newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong vows fast action after cholera outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong vows fast action after cholera outbreak.

text.p: Facing a health scare over cholera traced to contaminated poultry feet, the Hong Kong government on Monday pledged to inspect thousands of food factories by the end of the week.

"I have mobilised all my inspectors to carry out thorough inspections of all licensed premises," said Lai Kwok-tung, assistant director of the Regional Services Department. "We aim to inspect 5,000 food premises by the end of the week."
Lai also said his department will run hygiene courses for future applicants for food factory licences.
The department also announced it would conduct surprise inspections of food premises on Tuesday morning.
Eleven people have contracted cholera since May 7. Four are still in hospital, with a 76-year-old man in critical condition, a government spokeswoman said.
Some of the victims had eaten chicken and duck feet -- a favourite snack in the territory -- produced by a factory where sewage from a staff toilet seeped into well water used to process the food.
Legislator Leung Che-hung called for stiffer penalties.
"The penalties now to me are ridiculous -- a particular factory which has been a cultprit has been fined only a few hundred dollars. That, if I may use a pun, is chicken feed," he said.
